0.content:
Illuga is a young, upright Ratnik and squad leader, adopted son of Starshyna Nikita. Worried that Flins will die alone on his island, he regularly brings supplies and work documents, and politely needles him with questions. Why is Flins never thirsty? Why does he only appear at night? How does he come and go without being seen? Flins calls him "Young Master" for wrapping curiosity in such good manners. He spins him half-finished stories about fae nobles and gems, and admires Illuga's determination above wit or cunning.

Flins once told Illuga he had bought a gem at an auction; the auction house had never heard of it. Flins hinted that "distant relatives" might send Illuga a gemstone of his own someday (a Moon Wheel). In 6.3 Flins asked Illuga to organise the Lightkeepers' evacuations and admitted he had been "cursed". Furious, Illuga asked outright whether Flins is human. Flins feigned ignorance; Illuga said he would ask again once it was over, and told him to come back alive.

After Dottore's defeat Flins persuaded a nervous Illuga to become the Lightkeepers' representative in the new League, someone "upright" who cares about others, and told him "You know the truth now." Illuga's own voice-over says he has a rough idea of Flins's secret, and that a non-answer is itself an answer. In an anecdote, Flins admits he arranged for Aino to attend a big headquarters meeting as part of a "trick" to make absences less conspicuous (a single falling leaf draws the eye, a flurry does not); Illuga complains he is usually the only one left in the room.

1.content:
Before he was a Ratnik, Flins was Kyryll Chudomirovich Flins, a fae noble of the Snezhnayan court in the era of the Belyi Tsar. Legend calls him Kyryll the Azure Flame and says he began as a blue flame guiding fallen souls across the icy plains. He kept no followers and cared little for court balls, where friends, dance partners and antiques were all "second-hand". He was present for the handover of power to the Tsaritsa, then vanished.

Rumour gives several reasons: dissatisfaction with the Tsar or Tsaritsa, an imprudent word and a purge, or simply that his fire went out. His crest and surname remain in the register of nobility. As Flins, he tells "the legend of Kyryll" in the third person, praises its atmosphere, and claims "Flins" is a coincidental surname. To the Traveler he says he was once addressed as "Chudomirovich" and that his long hair was a mark of status.

2.comment: Flins: The Long Sleep and the Final Night Cemetery
2.content:
After leaving court Kyryll drifted south by rail and chose a small isle in Nod-Krai as his "tomb". He laid stone slates, built an altar, sealed himself in with ancient rites, became a ball of fire and sank into the earth. Hundreds of years later, Lightkeepers fought the Wild Hunt above him. A dying warrior traced the fae script with his own blood and begged for help, and the azure flame woke. Flins fought beside them, but he was weak from sleep and many died. He and the survivors buried the dead, and the isle became the Final Night Cemetery. He lives there alone in the old lighthouse.

Flins dates it to several decades ago; by Lightkeeper records nine in ten of the island's troops died, and the Ratniki had turned to the fabled "blue lantern" of local legend. The Lightkeepers later abandoned the island. The lighthouse holds a showroom of Lightkeeper records and his private collections, and a Ratniks' library he once used with the Traveler to unpick Rerir's plan.

In World Quests the Traveler relit the lighthouse. Flins said time had seemed frozen at the end of that battle, and lighting it had set time moving again. He does not mind. The lingering ghosts will return to the Ley Lines in time, and the fog will lift with them.

3.comment: Flins: Rerir's Heart and Flins's Lantern
3.content:
Every Lightkeeper carries an Oath Lantern, but Flins's is very old, non-standard, and burns a cold blue flame. After shattering a Wild Hunt core, he found a strange crystal and kept it in the lantern out of curiosity. More crystals merged with it, and it began leaking Abyssal energy that restricted his power and tormented him. He kept it rather than throw it away, reasoning it would do more harm in someone else's hands. It was a fragment of the heart of Rerir, one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, who was rebuilding himself from pieces of his corpse and was the source of the Wild Hunt.

The Traveler sensed something off about the lantern from their first meeting. They saved Flins from Rerir north of Nasha Town and cleansed the lantern. At Starsand Shoal Rerir revealed what the fragment was, absorbed the corrupted cannon blast and regained a partial body before Columbina rescued the group. Flins later handed the fragments to Nefer for the plan that trapped Rerir in 6.1. Rerir was flicked through a moon gate and thrown out of Teyvat.

4.comment: Flins: The Murder of Sergeant Major Sousi
4.content:
Sousi was a diligent Sergeant Major stationed in Nasha Town who kept waiting for a transfer home to his family. Rerir abducted him, impersonated him while Aino's kuuvahki cannon was repaired, then killed him wearing Flins's face before a witness. The Lightkeepers doubted Flins would do it, but the evidence looked damning. Flins swore to take Rerir's head.

Flins hid in his lantern so the Traveler could "pick him up" inside the guarded crime scene. Sousi's Aino-built mechanical arm was blinking a maintenance error, and the mechanic Hintsa confirmed Sousi had never collected his repair parts. So the "Sousi" at the cannon had been Rerir, whose shapeshifting copies only outward form. That night at The Flagship Flins confessed to the Traveler that he is fae. The next morning an angry mob came to The Flagship demanding to see him.

5.comment: Flins: Nikita, Olav and the Card Game
5.content: Flins once watched the night-watch Ratniki play cards for an hour before they noticed him. They offered to teach the "novice"; he deadlocked the table for hours, then lost on purpose to Olav, praising his patience. That gave Olav the confidence to accept Nikita's long-standing offer of a squad. Nikita knows Flins was a fae noble and has seen his collection. He came to thank him with supplies ("they can help you keep up the pretense") and lost repeatedly at cards: "Both are easier than pretending to be an ordinary person. Sorry, I win again."

6.content: Animals refuse to go near Flins, which Lauma noticed at once. She keeps her guard up but reserves judgment, shares the Enclave's harvest when he passes, and once spent twenty minutes at his door after bringing a Feast of the Moon he declined, saying he could not take up a faith. To Flins she calls to mind Hyperborea, "the bygone golden elysium", and he admires how she carries her heavy lineage and antlers.

7.content: Nefer, the Curatorium's boss, calls Flins a master of social distancing who wears etiquette like shining armour. Whether he is a Lightkeeper or a fae, from Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya, makes no difference to her; friendship rests on trust. He calls her intuition a knife no one wants to face and hopes she won't pry into his past, as he does not pry into hers. In 6.3 the two of them found Columbina's moonlit message at The Flagship.

8.comment: Flins: Collections and the Tear of the North
8.content: Flins collects old coins and gems for their scratches and stories, "much like a well-aged wine", and insists the hobby is not expensive. The Tear of the North, said to form from the courage of Snezhnayan soldiers and protect its bearer, was given to Kyryll by the Tsar. At the Deepwinter Cocktail Ball he lost it, on purpose, in a bet to a southern commoner named Sokolov. Generations later Sokolov's descendant, a struggling adventurer, sold it to Flins at ten percent above market value and confessed its noble origin. Flins praised them and sent them off confident, and only then let himself look at the long-lost gem.

9.content: Fae do not need Moon Wheels. Flins wears one because it matches his coat and explains his power. Human food tastes dull to him; he fakes enjoyment and feeds it to his lantern. He loves Snezhnaya's flaming Fire-Water and detests plain water. He is nocturnal ("The purpose of a lamp is to shine light into the darkness"), shows no breath in the cold, and can understand the Wild Hunt's servants. Snezhnaya was once the realm of the fae, he tells the Traveler. His race "is no longer of any importance", but he is proof it still exists. He suggests some fae stayed in Snezhnograd because they can no longer survive anywhere warm.

10.comment: Flins: Dottore's Curse and the True Moon
10.content: Everyone who went into Dottore's facility, Flins among them, carried a curse that Sandrone detected, and she expected it to trigger if they left Nod-Krai. Flins treated it lightly in front of Illuga, which made Illuga angrier. In the final battle Dottore sealed Flins, Lauma and Nefer in separate spaces. Columbina, back with the Traveler, freed them with the Iridescent Marrow, and the five overpowered Dottore, who was destroyed. Whether the curse lifted is not stated.

11.content: After Starsand Shoal, Columbina teleported Flins, the Traveler and others to Silvermoon Hall. Flins thanked "dear madame", asked her to call him Flins, and asked whether she had blocked the bolts heading for Hiisi Island. She said no; much later it turned out a future Columbina, travelling back through time, had done it. While the group planned a parting gift for her before Moon-Prayer Night, he suggested a lantern in case it was dark on the moon. On Moon-Prayer Night itself (6.2) he ran a sugar-sculpture stall in his true form, posing as "a talking magic lamp" that matched festival-goers to spirit animals, and asked the Traveler and Paimon to keep it "our little secret". He welcomed Columbina home as Moon Goddess and told her that her spirit animal was a free-spirited kuuhenki.

12.comment: Flins: Durin and the Phantoms of the Cataclysm
12.content: Before Moon-Prayer Night, mirage-like phantoms of the past appeared across Nod-Krai. Investigating with Durin and Albedo, Flins watched Durin try thirty-nine times to save people in an immutable vision of the cataclysm. He built a fire, offered water, and explained that the Abyss had ravaged Nod-Krai more than once: gods, fae and humans alike had been "grains of sand" before it. Asked how he could be so calm, he admitted he is six or seven hundred years old and saw it first-hand. He asked whether Durin's interest in the Abyss came from hatred or its call, noting he had carried Rerir's heart himself. He wished Durin well and asked him to keep their talk secret. When Nicole later tested candidates for the kuuvahki infusion needed to enter the Hyperborean ruins, he was ruled out as non-human.

13.content: Varka once came to the lighthouse to borrow supplies after monsters knocked his luggage over nearby, then rowed back to return them. Flins treats him like a tourist but says no sword in the world bites sharper than the North Wind. He calls Varka a true knight rarely seen these days, and says a sparring match with him would mean he was going up in the world. Varka, who disliked Old Mondstadt's aristocracy, says he would happily drink with aristocrats like Flins. In 6.4 the Traveler found Flins with Jahoda and Ineffa at the keep where Varka gathered allies against the new Wild Hunt attacks.

14.content: Jahoda once turned up at the lighthouse claiming to be on business for the Curatorium. In truth she was lost, and Flins had already saved her from falling off a cliff without her noticing. He says she is learning the philosophy of survival from Nod-Krai itself. She wonders whether he knows of untouched ruins but would never ask. Aino compares his speech to the clink-clank of fine machinery; he says their difference is not age but that he is hopeless with machines.

15.content: Behind ordinary document boxes in the lighthouse showroom are Flins's "Skeleton Jigsaws": miniature skeletons he hand-carves from beast fangs, ancient fossils and sterilised monster carapaces, assembled into the monsters he has fought in Nod-Krai. Each part answers a moment in combat. A finished model is boxed and labelled with the date and opponent, and he is in a good mood for having "solved" another question. They are both a pastime and his blades for dissecting the Wild Hunt.

key: The winds awaken the leaves whirl round
16.content: The oath sworn by those joining the Lightkeepers begins "The winds awaken, the leaves whirl round". A Lightkeeper abandons their lantern only when they have no other choice, so every masterless Oath Lantern marks a tragedy; Flins says the least the living can do is remember the oaths. He approves of the Lightkeepers' three cardinal virtues: prudence, modesty and loyalty. He says the role of Ratnik suits a nocturnal being who can frighten other creatures of the night. He notes that Lightkeepers do not habitually say "Her Majesty, the Tsaritsa", and that by "us" he means the Lightkeepers, of course.

17.content: Each snowfall, Flins says, is Snezhnaya calling. He recalls an age when fae and humans roamed it freely and once thought they shared an ancestry; now he believes what unites them is a common spirit, "the spirit that gives rise to all things good and kind". His memories of Snezhnograd are hazy: a brilliant night sky, an endless blizzard. He has heard it is industrialised now, and wonders what it looks like. Knowing the Traveler would head on to Snezhnaya, he wished them a safe trip and called its snowy plains beautiful.
